items.title: CONSENT CALENDAR
Contract No. WW-795, Sansome Street Outfall Improvements, to R&S Construction Management, Inc., to rehabilitate the Sansome Street Outfall
items.text: Award Contract No. WW-795, Sansome Street Outfall Improvements, to the responsible bidder that submitted the lowest responsive bid, R&S Construction Management, Inc., in the amount of $3,322,700 and with a duration of 300 consecutive calendar days (approximately 10 months), to rehabilitate the Sansome Street Outfall, located in the City and County of San Francisco. This action constitutes the Approval Action for the Project for the purposes of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), pursuant to San Francisco Administrative Code section 31.04(h). The Planning Department has determined that the Project is exempt from the CEQA. The Commission will rely on that determination to make its decision on this action

items.title: Designate Evoqua Tow Brow® secondary clarifier mechanism, as the sole source product for Contract No. DB-140, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant - Secondary Clarifiers Rehabilitation
items.text: Authorize the General Manager to designate Evoqua Tow Brow® secondary clarifier mechanism, as the sole source product for Contract No. DB-140, Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant - Secondary Clarifiers Rehabilitation, to match existing products used at San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Southeast Water Pollution Control Plant, in conformance with San Francisco Administrative Code Section 6.73(e) and California Public Contract Code Section 3400(c)(2)

items.title: Adopt (1) new Rules and Regulations Governing Hydrant Use for Temporary Water Supply, and (2) associated amendments to the Rules and Regulations Governing Water Service to Customers
items.text: Public hearing to consider and possible action to adopt (1) new Rules and Regulations Governing Hydrant Use for Temporary Water Supply, and (2) associated amendments to the Rules and Regulations Governing Water Service to Customers, in conformance with the requirements of Charter Section 4.104; and authorize the General Manager to approve any non-substantive amendments or minor corrections to the Rules and Regulations Governing Hydrant Use for Temporary Water Supply that the General Manager, in consultation with the City Attorney, determines are necessary or appropriate to facilitate implementation of the Hydrant Use Permit Program

items.title: Agreements with the City of Daly City
items.text: Approve the terms and conditions and authorize the General Manager and/or City’s Director of Property to execute certain agreements with the City of Daly City, consisting of (i) a License Amendment to extend the term of SFPUC License No. P4703 for Habitat Mitigation, Monitoring, and Facilities by an additional five years, for a total of 10 years and four months, for an additional use fee of $23,503 and a total use fee of $51,015; (ii) a 50-year License Agreement to construct, operate, and maintain SFPUC-owned overflow facilities at Lake Merced for a total use fee of $2,278 on a 9,286-square-foot portion of San Francisco Assessor’s Parcel No. 7283-004, designated as SFPUC Parcel No. 55 (Lake Merced Tract); and (iii) a Purchase and Sale Agreement, Quitclaim Deed, and Easement Deed for the quitclaim of two existing SFPUC tunnel easements totaling 46,992 square feet on San Francisco Assessor’s Parcels: Nos. 7284-001, 7284-003, 7282- 005 and 7282-006, and the sale of five easements for stormwater facilities totaling approximately 180,010 square feet for a total purchase price of $71,000 on SFPUC Parcel No. 55, subject to Board of Supervisors and Mayor approval

items.title: Increase to the cost contingency and duration contingency for Contract No. WD-2794B, Sunol Long Term Improvements Alameda Creek Watershed Center, with S.J. Amoroso Construction Co.
items.text: Approve an increase of $500,000 to the cost contingency and an increase of 910 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. WD-2794B, Sunol Long Term Improvements Alameda Creek Watershed Center, with S.J. Amoroso Construction Co., for a revised cost limit of $36,905,700 and a revised duration limit of 3,033 consecutive calendar days (approximately seven years and ten months), to provide time to complete the fabrication, installation, and corrective actions related to the redesigned exhibits and to investigate and address water leaks within the facility, including potential additional extended overhead costs related to the redesign of the exhibits and time to cover the post- construction maintenance services that were included in the original contract scope

items.title: Increase to the cost contingency and duration contingency for Contract No. HH-1015, O’Shaughnessy Dam Drainage and Miscellaneous Improvements, with Sierra Mountain Construction, Inc.
items.text: Approve an increase of $1,000,000 to the cost contingency and an increase of 382 calendar days to the duration contingency for Contract No. HH-1015, O’Shaughnessy Dam Drainage and Miscellaneous Improvements, with Sierra Mountain Construction, Inc., for a revised cost limit of $6,814,550 and a revised duration limit of 778 calendar days (approximately two years and two months), to address modifications to the ladder- well platforms necessary to conform to site conditions and additional crack sealing work in supply wells to reduce leakage and thereby improve safe access within the dam. Jimmy Leong, Project Manager Bureau Principal Engineer-Hetchy Capital Improvement

items.title: COMMUNICATIONS
Items initiated by Commissioners
items.text: Items initiated by Commissioners (discussion only) Commissioner Stacy inquired about having a hearing on the Bay Delta Plan amendment and the Healthy Rivers and Landscapes (HRL) Program in 2026. General Manager Herrera clarified and confirmed that a presentation for the Bay Delta Plan and its HRL Program interaction will be delivered during the 2026 calendar year. Commissioner Stacy commented on correspondence and testimony received by the Commission relating to concerns about synthetic turf at Crocker Amazon Park; its effect on groundwater, wastewater and drinking water streams; and, stated interest for the PUC to be involved in discussions. GM Herrera explained that the San Francisco Recreation and Parks Department is the lead on the Crocker Amazon discussions and stated that the SFPUC is not involved
